This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this project is

A modular R workflow for delineating stream and lake catchments across multiple sites in Canada and computing morphometric metrics. It is project-agnostic: the user supplies a sites table and paths to shared external datasets; the workflow produces self-contained per-site output folders.

All code is plain R scripts sourced interactively — there is no build system, package install step, or test runner. There are no automated tests.

## Running the workflow

There is one runner per project, both on the shared `workflow/` layout:

- `workflow/run_celeste.R` — CELESTE stream/river sites
- `workflow/run_cam_lakes.R` — CAM lake sites

Each is sourced interactively in R (or run section-by-section), not executed as a CLI script.

```r
# From an R session in the project root:
source("workflow/run_celeste.R")
```

Before running, set the path variables near the top of that file (MRDEM VRT, NHN directory, NHN index shapefile, HydroBasins directory) and point it at your sites source.

To reset outputs selectively before a rerun:

```r
source("code/reset_workflow.R")
reset_site("site_id")          # one site only
reset_group("group_id", sites) # one group cache + its sites
reset_sites(sites)             # all site outputs, keep cache
reset_all()                    # everything
```

To rerun watershed delineation for a single site after editing its pour point in QGIS:

```r
source("workflow/R/stream/99_rerun_sites")     # defines rerun_site_watershed()
rerun_site_watershed("site_id", sites, group_manifest, output_dir)
```

## Architecture

### Two-tier processing structure

Processing is split into **groups** (hydrologically coherent regions sharing a DEM) and **sites** (individual pour points). The key insight is that expensive DEM conditioning (breach depressions, flow accumulation) runs once per group, not once per site.

- A **group** is identified by `group_id` in the sites table. All sites sharing a group share a DEM crop and all WhiteboxTools outputs.
- A **site** is a single pour point. Multiple sites can share a group if they fall within the same HydroBasins level-6 polygon(s).

### Module sequence (`workflow/R/`)

Stream/river-specific modules live in `workflow/R/stream/`; lake-specific modules in `workflow/R/lake/`. `utils.R` and Stages 06–08 are shared by both pipelines.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `utils.R` | Logging (`cw_inform/warn/abort`), site validation, AOI construction, file-system helpers |
| `stream/01_group_sites.R` | Builds the `group_manifest` sf tibble; creates `cache/<group_id>/` and `output/<site_id>/` directories |
| `stream/02_prepare_dem.R` | Crops MRDEM VRT to each group AOI → `cache/<group_id>/dem.tif` |
| `stream/03_burn_streams.R` | Reads NHN GDB files, merges flowlines/waterbodies, optionally burns streams into DEM → `flowlines.gpkg`, `waterbodies.gpkg`, `dem_burned.tif` |
| `stream/04_run_whitebox.R` | Breach → D8 pointer → accumulation → stream extraction → hillshade → `dem_breached.tif`, `flow_pointer.tif`, `flow_accum.tif`, `streams.tif`, `hillshade.tif` |
| `stream/05_delineate_sites.R` | Snap pour point → watershed delineation → polygon conversion → clip all group rasters to each catchment → per-site outputs |
| `stream/99_rerun_sites` | Defines `rerun_site_watershed()` for fixing individual sites post-delineation without clearing the full group cache |
| `stream/06_hydroweight_attributes.R` | Distance-weighted catchment attributes (hydroweight), pour point as the O-scheme target, for both catchment versions. Analogous lake logic (lake polygon as O target) lives in `lake/05_hydroweight_attributes.R` |
| `06_remove_upstream.R` | For nested sites: erases smaller upstream catchments from larger downstream ones → `catchment_clipped.gpkg` (stream); analogous lake logic lives in `lake/04_remove_upstream_lakes.R` |
| `07_reclip_outputs.R` | Re-clips all rasters and flowlines to the clipped catchment polygon → `*_clipped.tif` / `streams_clipped.gpkg`. Shared — works for stream (`group_manifest`) or lake (`cache_dir`) projects |
| `08_catchment_metrics.R` | Computes geometry, areal, relief, and (when applicable) lake/stream morphometric metrics following Shekar & Mathew (2024), for both unclipped and clipped catchments |

### Hydroweight (distance-weighted catchment attributes)

Both projects use the `hydroweight` package to compute inverse-distance-weighted landscape attributes (e.g. % land cover, mean NDVI) under seven weighting schemes (`lumped`, `iEucO`, `iFLO`, `HAiFLO`, `iEucS`, `iFLS`, `HAiFLS`). The two pipelines differ only in what the "O" (outflow) target is:

- **Lake** (`lake/05_hydroweight_attributes.R`): `target_O` = the lake polygon. `remove_region` excises the lake's own footprint from LOI summaries (it has area). Uses one project-wide DEM/flow accumulation raster (single contiguous region).
- **Stream** (`stream/06_hydroweight_attributes.R`): `target_O` = the site's pour point (`output/<site_id>/pour_point.gpkg`) — a point has no `remove_region`. DEM/flow accumulation are resolved **per site from that site's group cache** (`cache_dir/<group_id>/`), since CELESTE groups span separate HydroBasins regions with independent DEMs. Runs for both `catchment.gpkg` and `catchment_clipped.gpkg`, tagged by a `version` column.

`loi_layers[[i]]` supports exactly one of three source shapes:
- `path` — a single raster already covering the full site extent (reprojected + cached once, up front).
- `path_template` — one pre-clipped raster per site, containing a literal `"{site_id}"` placeholder. Only needs to cover the unclipped catchment; the clipped-version pass crops it down further. Resolved lazily per site.
- `path_lazy` — one shared source too large to reproject/cache whole (e.g. a mosaic VRT over scattered regional tiles, or a rasterized-per-group vector layer, whose combined bounding box is much bigger than the actual data coverage). May contain a literal `"{group_id}"` and/or `"{site_id}"` placeholder for a source that varies per group/site (e.g. one rasterized harvest/regen layer per HydroBasins group). Cropped to each site's catchment *before* being reprojected or written to disk — never materializes the full source extent. Resolved lazily per site.

`workflow/raster_attributes.R` is a standalone, pipeline-independent utility (not sourced into either project's Stage sequence by default) for preparing LOI rasters ahead of time:
- `reclassify_categorical()` collapses/relabels raw categorical codes via a lookup table.
- `sens_slope_trend()` computes a per-pixel Theil-Sen slope + Mann-Kendall p-value across a raster time-series stack (e.g. annual NDVI) — deliberately without autocorrelation prewhitening (Yue-Pilon/Zhang), which was tested and found to meaningfully distort slope magnitude on short/noisy series; see the function's docstring for the empirical comparison.
- `check_tile_consistency()` reports CRS/resolution/band-count per file for a set of raster tiles — run before mosaicking to catch mismatches a VRT can't fix on its own.
- `build_mosaic_vrt()` mosaics scattered tiles into one VRT for use as `path_lazy`. Always sets `-vrtnodata` — without it, any area not covered by *any* input tile reads as `0`, not `NA`, which is indistinguishable from real data. Confirmed this empirically: CELESTE's `data/ndvi/*.tif` (12 regional NDVI tiles, 1984-2025, EPSG:3979) don't cover the NBE group (20 sites) at all — before the nodata fix this silently produced "NDVI = 0" for every NBE catchment; with it, those sites correctly fail the existing "all NA after crop/mask" check and are excluded from `hw_results`, not corrupted.
- `rasterize_competing_classes()` rasterizes several "class bucket" vector layers (e.g. every harvest-method gdb layer → "harvest", every regen-method layer → "regen") into one categorical raster, with temporal precedence between classes (most-recent-year wins, via `terra::rasterize(field = year_field, fun = "max")`) and one band per year plus one all-years-combined band. Used for `run_celeste.R`'s harvest/regen layer (Ontario only — `shared_data/raw/harvest/ontario_harvest.gdb`, NIP/TUR/KEN groups only, rasterized once per group).

`workflow/R/lake/01-05` (match lake polygons → prepare OIH DEM → delineate → remove upstream → hydroweight attributes) are lake-only and used solely by `run_cam_lakes.R`.

### Known terra / hydroweight quirks (found the hard way — read before touching multi-band categorical LOIs)

All confirmed by direct testing, not assumed, while building the harvest/regen layer (24 bands: 23 years + combined):

- **`terra::levels(r) <- df` on a multi-layer SpatRaster only applies to layer 1.** Layers 2+ silently keep `as.factor()`'s own auto-generated default labels — no error, no warning about *this* specific problem. Must be set per layer (`workflow/R/stream/06_hydroweight_attributes.R`'s `prepare_one_loi_raster()` does this, then rebuilds via `terra::rast(list(...))` — reassigning `names()` on the already-leveled multi-layer object afterwards silently wipes the levels back out again, so build each band as an independent single-layer raster and combine at the end, never mutate a multi-layer factor object in place).
- **`levels(single_layer) <- df` renames that layer to the attribute column's name** (e.g. "Class"), discarding whatever it was named before. This is *why* the per-layer-then-combine pattern above must also restore/reassign names during that same reconstruction, not after.
- **An exactly-3-band Byte GeoTIFF gets GDAL's automatic RGB photometric interpretation on write**, silently renaming bands to "red"/"green"/"blue" on every subsequent read. `writeRaster(..., gdal = "PHOTOMETRIC=MINISBLACK")` prevents it. Only bites a group whose data happens to produce exactly 3 bands (e.g. 2 years + combined) — real enough to guard against unconditionally.
- **`hydroweight_attributes()`'s raw categorical column format depends on the LOI's `names()`.** When it equals the `class_levels` attribute column name (e.g. "Class"), output is `"Class_{id}_{scheme}_prop"`. When it's anything else, output is `"{that_name}_{id}_{scheme}_prop"` instead — a different, easy-to-mis-parse format. `prep_categorical_for_hydroweight()` forces the name to the attribute column right before every call so the format is always the first, parseable one, independent of whatever the raster was named upstream for clarity (e.g. "y2015").
- **A categorical LOI with only one class actually present in the ROI produces an id-less column** (`"Class_{scheme}_prop"`, no class number) — ambiguous to parse, and every such layer produces the *same* raw names, so binding multiple degenerate layers collides. `single_class_value()` + `degenerate_categorical_table()` detect this and compute the answer directly instead of calling `hydroweight_attributes()`: a class covering 100% of the ROI has an exactly-1.0 distance-weighted proportion under *any* weighting scheme (indicator = 1 everywhere, so the weighted mean is `sum(weight)/sum(weight) = 1` regardless of the actual weights) — not an approximation.
- **A class with zero occurrences (but not the *only* class — some other class is present) is omitted from the output entirely**, not reported as 0. Fine for one site alone; once multiple sites/layers are bound together (always, in this pipeline) an omitted-for-this-row column becomes a misleading `NA` after `dplyr::bind_rows()`. `ensure_full_categorical_schema()` fills any such gap with an explicit 0 after cleaning.

Migrated from a river-only `R/*.R` layout (retired 2026-08, verified equivalent via `workflow/verify_stream_migration.R`) — see git history if you need the old structure.

### The `group_manifest` object

This sf tibble is the central data structure passed between modules. One row per group; columns: `group_id`, `burn_streams`, `buffer_m`, `aoi` (sfc geometry in EPSG:3979), `cache_dir`, `n_sites`. It is built by `build_group_manifest()` in Stage 1 and passed to every downstream stage.

### Caching

Every output file is checked with `cache_exists(path)` before writing. Re-running the workflow safely skips completed steps. To force a rerun, delete the relevant file or use the `reset_*()` helpers.

### CRS

All spatial outputs are in **EPSG:3979** (Canada Atlas Lambert NAD83(CSRS)), matching the MRDEM native CRS. No reprojection occurs in normal use.

### External data (not in repo)

| Dataset | Description |
|---|---|
| MRDEM `.vrt` | 30 m national DEM, streamed via VRT — no tile downloads |
| NHN GDB files | National Hydro Network per NTS sheet (`nhn_rhn_<sheet>_gdb_en/`) |
| NHN index shapefile | `NHN_INDEX_WORKUNIT_LIMIT_2.shp` — maps sheet codes to geometries |
| HydroBasins | `north_america/` and `arctic/` subdirectories, levels 1–12 `.shp` |

On Sam's machine these live under `~/Documents/cfs/shared_data/raw/`.

### Pour point correction

When a catchment looks wrong, the pour point snapped to the wrong stream cell. The fix:

1. Open `output/<site_id>/pour_point_snapped.shp` and `streams_tmp.tif` in QGIS
2. Edit `pour_point_snapped.shp` to move the point to the correct stream cell
3. Run `rerun_site_watershed()` (see above) — it reads the edited `.shp` directly without rerunning snapping

### Key design decisions

- **DEM is written as a rectangular crop, not masked to the AOI polygon.** Masking introduces NoData at AOI edges, which prevents WhiteboxTools from computing flow direction for those cells and produces incorrect catchments near the boundary.
- **`burn_streams` is a group-level flag**, not per-site. All sites in a group must share the same value.
- **HydroBasins region (na vs ar)** is resolved spatially by intersection with level-1 boundaries, not by latitude threshold.
- **`99_rerun_sites`** is a script (no `.R` extension) that defines `rerun_site_watershed()` for fixing individual sites post-delineation without clearing the full group cache.
- **`snap_pour_point()` always re-snaps from the raw point** — it has no cache check, so it will overwrite a manually-edited `pour_point_snapped.shp` if the normal delineation stage is rerun. Corrections must go through `rerun_site_watershed()`, which reads the edited `.shp` directly and skips snapping entirely.

# Catchment Workflow — Project Context

## Project overview
Reproducible R workflow to characterise lake and river catchments for water
quality modelling of post-industrial vegetation recovery in Sudbury, Ontario.
Two study systems: CAM lakes (45 sites) and CELESTE/river sites.

## Project structure
- `workflow/run_cam_lakes.R`                    — ACTIVE top-level runner for CAM lakes (Stages 1–7)
- `workflow/run_celeste.R`                      — ACTIVE top-level runner for CELESTE stream sites (Stages 1–9)
- `workflow/R/lake/05_hydroweight_attributes.R` — ACTIVE hydroweight module (lake Stage 7), target_O = lake polygon
- `workflow/R/stream/06_hydroweight_attributes.R` — ACTIVE hydroweight module (stream Stage 9), target_O = pour point
- `workflow/raster_attributes.R`                — Standalone LOI prep utility: reclassify_categorical(), sens_slope_trend(), build_mosaic_vrt(), rasterize_competing_classes()
- `workflow/R/stream/05_delineate_sites.R`      — River/stream site delineation
- `workflow/R/06_remove_upstream.R`             — River upstream clipping (shared module)
- `workflow/R/07_reclip_outputs.R`              — Reclip outputs to clipped catchment (shared, stream + lake)
- `workflow/R/08_catchment_metrics.R`           — Morphometric metrics, clipped + unclipped (shared, stream + lake)
- `R/*.R`, `code/delineate_catchments.R`        — SUPERSEDED (retired 2026-08) by the workflow/ layout above
- `hydroweight_debug.R`                         — Diagnostic script for hydroweight
- `upstream_network_test.R`                     — Experimental, abandoned

## CRS
EPSG:3161 (NAD83 / Ontario MNR Lambert) throughout — OIH native CRS.
Never reproject rasters during analysis.

## Key data paths (Mac)
- OIH Lakes:        /Users/sam/Documents/cfs/shared_data/raw/hydro/waterbodies/ON_waterbodies/ohn_waterbodies_valid.gpkg
- OIH DEM:          /Users/sam/Downloads/IntegratedHydrologyNE/EnforcedDEM.tif

- OIH Watercourse:  /Users/sam/Downloads/IntegratedHydrologyNE/IH_NE.gdb

## Key decisions
- Flow direction: OIH Enhanced Flow Direction recoded to Whitebox encoding
  (one-step clockwise rotation: OIH 128→WBT 1, 1→2, 2→4, 4→8, 8→16, 16→32, 32→64, 64→128)
- Pour points: buffered lake polygon (30 m) rasterized to FULL D8 extent (no trim before wbt_watershed)
- Upstream area threshold: 4 ha minimum based on OIH lake polygon area (not catchment area)
- Excluded waterbody types: Pond
- CANLCC is reprojected once to EPSG:3161 and cached to cache/CAM/hydroweight_loi/canlcc_reprojected.tif
  by prepare_loi_layers() in 05_hydroweight_attributes.R (terra temp file GC avoidance)
- Stream rasters passed to hydroweight() as target_S are extended to the full DEM extent
  via terra::extend() so flow-path distances can be computed across the entire catchment domain

## R style preferences
- tidyverse style with native pipe |>
- Well-commented for reproducibility
- Section headings use ---- style (RStudio/Positron outline compatible)
- PROJECT_ID namespaces all output/cache paths
